text.p: Scandals and squabbling are threatening to hinder Bayern Munich's campaign to win a record 14th German championship.

Annoyed by intense media attention, the German league leaders have felt it necessary to put up a fence at their training ground to keep journalists away from the players as they prepare for Saturday's home clash with Werder Bremen.
Last week's announcement that German captain Juergen Klinsmann is leaving at the end of the season because he does not fit in has opened a can of worms at a club which has a reputation for scandals.
Klinsmann's decision proved that Bayern still have about as much harmony in the dressing rooms as a group of tone-deaf drunks at the city's beer festival.
The players are reported to be worried that they have a mole in their ranks who is leaking details of private discussions and incidents to the outside world.
"What had been going on here over the past few weeks couldn't continue," Bayern general manager Uli Hoeness said of the media blackout.
"It was a permanent television show, almost as if they had taken over the training ground. The players couldn't even get to their cars. We had to put a stop to it."
Germany's biggest sports magazine Sport Bild reported on Wednesday that Klinsmann was part of a group who tried to bring down Lothar Matthaeus as club captain.
Germany's former World Cup captain Matthaeus, who is widely known to have had disagreements with Klinsmann, admitted he had refused to wear the captain's armband during a recent league game.

"I was completely down after the (players') meeting," Matthaeus said. "I noticed from the reaction of some of the players that they still trusted me. But I said to myself: 'If someone else wants the armband they should demand it'.

Club chairman Franz Beckenbauer was also very critical of the team in public after two poor performances in the last few weeks. It is clear that Beckenbauer's other jobs as a television pundit and newspaper columnist can make life difficult for the club.
"We are going to re-think our policy towards the media completely before next season," Beckenbauer said.

Bayern have a two-point lead at the top after a 2-0 victory at Karlsruhe last Sunday. Klinsmann, who missed the win because of suspension, was given a short holiday by coach Giovanni Trapattoni but is expected to return against 10th-placed Bremen.
Because of the Easter weekend, Bundesliga action has been split between Thursday and Saturday with no games scheduled for Good Friday or Easter Sunday.
Reigning champions Borussia Dortmund lost ground in the race when they suffered their first home defeat of the season at the hands of Borussia Moenchengladbach last weekend.
Dortmund, who have slipped to fourth, have a chance to make up points on Thursday when they visit struggling St. Pauli.
Second-placed VfB Stuttgart are at home to 1860 Munich on the same night. Third-placed Bayer Leverkusen play fifth-placed Schalke on Saturday.
